simple.meaning: פָּחַז (pâchaz) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to bubble up or froth (as boiling water), i.e. (figuratively) to be unimportant.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Judges, Zephaniah, beginning at Judges 9:4. The surrounding contexts include Torah, priesthood, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּחַז (H6348) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פָּחַז (pâchaz) / H6348 is traced through Judges 9:4, Zephaniah 3:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.
